title: OpenAI ChatCompletions canonicalizer v2 - streaming + tool-call mapping
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Implement a robust canonicalization layer that maps incoming OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response semantics into Redwood's internal request model with correct streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured-output behavior.

Scope:
- Translate OpenAI 'messages' -> Redwood message frames including role/name handling, metadata, and content-types.
- Support OpenAI streaming deltas and map them to Redwood streaming frames without losing function_call or structured output boundaries.
- Map OpenAI function_call behaviors (explicit name, 'auto', or 'none') to Redwood tool invocation primitives, including partial arg streams and finalization.
- Provide backward-compatible error mapping (rate limits, model unavail, invalid tool args) and actionable SDK errors.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting SDKs beyond small helpers for edge cases (we'll keep SDK surface stable).
- Supporting deprecated OpenAI parameters that have no Redwood equivalent unless there is clear customer demand.

Constraints & considerations:
- Streaming: OpenAI streams often emit 'delta' events that mix content and function_call.name/arguments. We must reconstruct deterministic final messages for metrics, caching, and audits.
- Caching/KV: partial streams should not be cached as complete responses. Only fully-committed responses may populate prefix/KV caches.
- Tool args size: some tools are invoked with very large JSON arg blobs split across many deltas. We need a memory-efficient assembler and guardrails to avoid OOM on maliciously large streams.
- Rollout: ship behind feature-flag per-customer to allow gradual opt-in.

Design proposal (summary):
1) Input canonicalizer: single-pass parser that converts OpenAI request into Redwood canonical request. Handles role/name mapping, merges duplicate system messages, normalizes content types (text, json, structured), and extracts intent for tool-calling hints.
2) Streaming proxy: stream events are tokenized into 'stream-chunks' with metadata fields {message_id, role, boundary, partial_function_call_name?, partial_function_args?}. We emit these into Redwood runtime stream; the runtime reconstructs final message on commit.
3) Function/tool call handling: we introduce a 2-phase commit for tool calls triggered by OpenAI 'function_call' signals. If OpenAI stream signals function_call in progress, we start a 'tool-session' reserved for the request and accept incremental args. On finalization, we invoke tool adapter. If the model switches to 'text' mid-stream, we abort tool session and convert captured args into an error-details frame for observability.
4) Structured output enforcement: when a model promises structured output via function signature or schema, we perform lightweight validation server-side (schema existence, JSON parse) and return structured-error frames to the client rather than generic 500s.

Operational safeguards:
- Max tool-args size: default 2MB per request (configurable per-customer).
- Stream assembly timeout: if function_call argument stream stalls >5s, mark partial and keep alive based on customer SLAs.
- Telemetry: instrument event-level traces to link streaming deltas to final message and tool invocations for debugging and cost attribution.

Migration & compatibility:
- Map existing OpenAI-style requests to canonicalized calls by default. New canonicalizer behind feature flag 'openai_cc_v2_canonicalizer'.
- SDK changes: add opt-in helpers in JS/Go SDK to translate Redwood streaming events back to OpenAI delta shape for customers that expect native deltas.

Deliverables:
- Canonicalizer service + streaming proxy implementation (Go), unit + integration tests.
- SDK helpers (JS + Python) and sample app demonstrating tool-call streaming.
- Docs + migration guide in the Console and DevDocs.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions requests are deterministically mapped to Redwood canonical requests (unit tests covering role/name/content variants).
Streaming deltas from OpenAI are emitted to Redwood streams with sufficient metadata to reconstruct final messages and function calls (integration test).
Function/tool call sessions assemble partial arg streams safely and invoke tool adapters only after finalization (load-tested against large arg blobs).
SDK helpers return OpenAI-like delta events when feature-flag enabled and do not break existing Redwood SDK behavior.
Telemetry traces link streamed deltas -> final message -> tool invocation in the Console for at least 90% of sampled requests.
No regressions in existing non-OpenAI endpoints as validated by automated acceptance suite.
